claim.pdf_says:
15.12.2   General format

FUNCTION  BASECONVERT  ( argument-1  argument-2  argument-3 )      [FUNCTION and BASECONVERT are both UNDERLINED in the printed general format]
claim.markdown_says:
### 15.12.2 General format

FUNCTION BASECONVERT ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining in a general format is normative notation (5.2.6): an underlined word is a REQUIRED word. The transcription emits the format as bare prose with no underline markup at all. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34228. BASECONVERT is a COBOL-2023 addition, so this is precisely the kind of format an implementer reads fresh; losing the required-word marking removes the only signal distinguishing required words from optional keywords.

verdict.reasoning:
Attempted refutation on every available ground and the claim survived all of them.

(1) Both quotations are accurate. Rendered specs page 851 (printed folio 821) at 300 dpi and cropped the general-format line. The printed glyphs read 'FUNCTION  BASECONVERT  ( argument-1  argument-2  argument-3 )', and there are two distinct horizontal rules below the baseline: one spanning exactly the eight characters of FUNCTION, a separate one spanning exactly the eleven characters of BASECONVERT. The rules are broken between the two words and stop before the opening parenthesis. Neither the parentheses nor argument-1/-2/-3 is underlined. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:34228 is verbatim 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )' with no <u> tags, no bold, and not even a code fence or backticks.

(2) Not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture. The words themselves are all present and in the right order; the loss is purely the typographic layer, and that layer is normative here.

(3) Not an unrepresentable-notation excuse. The transcription already HAS a convention for this and applies it: the immediately preceding function on the facing page, 15.11.2 ATAN, is transcribed '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ATAN</u> ( argument-1 )'. 20 of the 94 chapter-15 general formats carry <u> markup. So the markup was available and was simply dropped here.

(4) The meaning change is real, and is worse than the claim states. Underlining is not merely a 'signal' whose absence is neutral: 8.3.2.4.2 Required words says 'Keywords. Within each format, such words are uppercase and underlined', and 8.3.2.4.3 Optional words says 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format' (mirrored by 5.2.2 and 5.2.3). Because the standard assigns a positive meaning to the ABSENCE of an underline, stripping it does not degrade the format to ambiguous, it inverts it: a reader applying 8.3.2.4.3 to the transcribed line concludes that both FUNCTION and BASECONVERT are optional words that may be omitted with no semantic effect. That is a false, and syntactically consequential, reading of a general format.

(5) The claim's premise about novelty holds. Annex-level change list at line 1230 lists 'BASECONVERT function' under 'The following intrinsic functions were added or enhanced', and line 49754 records 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT. This function has been added to enable conversion between different number bases in the range 2-16.' So it is a 2023 addition read without prior familiarity, as claimed.

The only defects in the claim are a misattributed citation and an understated scope, neither of which rescues the transcription. Verdict: genuine structural discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, with two corrections to the write-up.

Correction 1 - wrong section cited. The claim attributes the underline convention to 5.2.6. 5.2.6 is 'Options' and governs brackets, braces, choice indicators and ellipses, not underlining. The normative basis for underlining is 5.2.2 (Keywords: 'shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats ... required') with its complement 5.2.3 (Optional words: 'shown in uppercase and not underlined'), restated normatively in 8.3.2.4.2 Required words and 8.3.2.4.3 Optional words.

Correction 2 - understated scope. This is not specific to BASECONVERT or to newly added 2023 functions. 74 of the 94 '15.x.2 General format' blocks in the transcription carry no <u> markup anywhere in the block; only 20 do. Affected entries include long-standing 1985/2002 functions (FACTORIAL 15.36.2, INTEGER 15.44.2, MOD 15.64.2, NUMVAL 15.67.2, REM 15.77.2, REVERSE 15.78.2, SQRT 15.84.2, WHEN-COMPILED 15.99.2) alongside the newer ones. BASECONVERT should be filed as one instance of a systemic chapter-15 defect, and the remediation should be a sweep of all 74, not a one-line patch.

Correction 3 - sharpen the impact statement. The consequence is not that the required/optional distinction is 'removed'; it is that it is REVERSED. 8.3.2.4.3 gives the absence of an underline a positive meaning, so an unmarked uppercase word in a general format affirmatively reads as an optional word omittable with no semantic effect. The transcribed line therefore asserts something false about FUNCTION and BASECONVERT rather than merely omitting something true.

Secondary observation, worth noting for the sweep: 15.12.2 is additionally the bare-prose variant. Sibling non-underlined entries at least wrap the format in backticks or a fence (15.13.2 '`FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1 argument-2 )`'), which preserves the this-is-a-general-format-not-narrative cue. 15.12.2 has neither underline nor code formatting, so it is the weakest form of the defect. Corrected target text: '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>BASECONVERT</u> ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )', matching the 15.11.2 ATAN precedent already in the file.
